name: Pediatric arthroscopic approach for distal-femoral epiphyseal fractures
aliases: pediatric knee arthroscopy for epiphyseal fracture
region: pediatric knee and distal femoral epiphysis
corridor: Standard anterolateral viewing and anteromedial working portals beside the patellar tendon

positioning.text: Position supine with a thigh support and freely mobile knee, preserving access for percutaneous fixation and fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Use only with arthroscopic expertise; prepare low-pressure irrigation, pediatric instruments, percutaneous fixation, and fluoroscopy before portal placement.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark patella, patellar-tendon borders, joint lines, femoral condyles, tibial tubercle, and anteromedial and anterolateral soft spots.

incision.text: Create approximately 5-mm anterolateral and anteromedial stab incisions at the palpated soft spots adjacent to the patellar tendon.

superficial_interval.text: Bluntly spread each portal tract and establish the medial portal under direct arthroscopic control.

deep_interval.text: Insert a blunt trocar and sleeve gently, clear hemarthrosis, inspect the epiphyseal reduction, and manipulate only under direct visualization.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, retinacular capsule, synovium, then pediatric knee articular cavity.

structures_encountered.text: Patellar tendon, fat pad, cartilage, menisci, cruciate ligaments, distal-femoral physis and epiphyseal fracture are assessed.

structures_at_risk.text: Articular cartilage, menisci, cruciates, patellar tendon, open physis, portal-adjacent nerves, and posterior neurovascular structures are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid sharp intra-articular advancement and excessive pump pressure; capsular disruption can cause fluid extravasation and compartment syndrome.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not lever instruments on pediatric cartilage or the physis; add a visualized accessory portal rather than forcing trajectory.

exposure.text: Provides magnified articular-reduction assessment and survey for associated meniscal, ligament, and osteochondral injury.

limitations.text: Recommended only for minimally or nondisplaced fractures; displaced, comminuted, or unstable patterns generally require open control.

extensions.text: Add a portal under visualization or convert promptly to an open pediatric lateral or parapatellar exposure when reduction cannot be controlled.

indications.text: Consider for selected minimally or nondisplaced distal-femoral epiphyseal fractures when direct surface assessment improves reduction confidence.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid with major displacement, comminution, uncontrolled capsular leakage, infection, or unavailable pediatric arthroscopic expertise.

implant_implications.text: Plan fixation to restore epiphyseal anatomy while minimizing avoidable physeal violation and keeping implants outside cartilage.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Combine surface visualization with orthogonal and tangential imaging to confirm physis, reduction, trajectory, length, and joint containment.

closure.text: Drain irrigation, confirm soft compartments and hemostasis, and close portal skin incisions routinely.

complications.text: Complications include chondral injury, extravasation or compartment syndrome, infection, stiffness, fixation loss, and growth arrest or deformity.

bailouts.text: Stop pump inflow and convert to open exposure if extravasation progresses or stable anatomic reduction cannot be obtained.

procedure_applications.condition: A minimally or nondisplaced epiphyseal fracture is suitable for arthroscopy-assisted assessment and fixation by an experienced pediatric knee arthroscopist

questions.question: Which fractures are candidates?
questions.answer: Selected minimally or nondisplaced epiphyseal fractures.

questions.question: What associated injuries should be surveyed?
What pump complication is especially important?
questions.answer: Fluid extravasation and compartment syndrome when the capsule is ruptured.
